title: IQM's New CTO Sees Quantum Computing Shift From Lab To Market
excerpt: IQM’s new CTO, Dr. Craig Ciesla, details the quantum computing shift from academic theory to delivering real-world products to customers globally.
content:
The challenge in quantum computing has decisively shifted, according to IQM’s new Chief Technology Officer, Dr. Craig Ciesla, from simply proving the technology works to now aggressively scaling it for real-world use. Ciesla, who previously translated scientific advances into products in fibre-optic communications and life sciences, highlights that IQM is uniquely positioned to meet this challenge by building the entire quantum computing stack, hardware, chips, software and applications, the company says.

“What I’ve always found most interesting isn’t the idea in the lab,” Ciesla explains, “It’s the moment the idea leaves it, finds its customers and starts solving real problems,” a shift reflected by systems already being delivered to customers globally.

CTO Ciesla Transitions Quantum Computing from Research to Product

IQM is building a complete quantum computing stack, a strategy that distinguishes it from competitors focused on single components, according to its new Chief Technology Officer, Dr. Craig Ciesla. This full-stack approach allows the company to address customer problems holistically, rather than optimizing individual parts in isolation, a point Ciesla emphasized during his initial weeks with the organization, according to IQM. He noted that IQM’s ambition extends beyond incremental improvements, aiming to deliver comprehensive solutions encompassing hardware, chips, software and applications.

Ciesla’s arrival at IQM signals a shift within the quantum computing industry; the focus is now firmly on scaling systems for practical use, rather than solely proving the underlying technology functions. He observed that many quantum systems have already been constructed and are actively being used by customers globally, indicating the field’s maturation.

This transition, from theoretical exploration to tangible application, was a key factor in his decision to join the company, as he has consistently sought opportunities to translate scientific advancements into real-world products throughout his career. He described encountering a team of dedicated physicists, but was even more struck by their determination to not only publish research, but to build the technology that will define the future of quantum computing.

This combination of intellectual rigor and practical focus, he believes, is a rare and valuable asset. Ciesla intends to focus on removing obstacles for these teams, clarifying priorities, accelerating decision-making and enabling individuals to use their expertise effectively, the company says. IQM’s approach to innovation embraces experimentation and risk-taking, recognizing that unsuccessful experiments are not failures, but valuable sources of information. Ciesla believes that supporting an environment where individuals feel safe to challenge assumptions and explore unconventional ideas is essential for sustained breakthroughs.

He sees balancing this exploratory spirit with the need for consistent execution as one of the defining challenges for IQM in the coming years. The company is currently delivering products while simultaneously investigating what future quantum capabilities might look like, a dual focus that demands a unique organizational structure and mindset. Ciesla’s initial focus has been on understanding the existing strengths and challenges within IQM, prioritizing active listening and inquiry over immediate directives.

He emphasized that understanding precedes direction, and that his role is to facilitate the work of the already remarkable team. This emphasis on people extends beyond technical expertise. Ciesla believes that brilliant ideas require brilliant teams to become successful products, teams built on trust, shared understanding, and a sense of purpose. He noted that every breakthrough he has witnessed in his career has ultimately been driven by the people involved.

The transition to IQM also represents a personal shift for Ciesla and his family, with relocations across multiple countries and ongoing educational pursuits for his children. He described a lifelong curiosity that extends beyond his professional life, finding fulfillment in travel, music, and exploring new environments. This personal drive for discovery, he suggests, aligns perfectly with the spirit of innovation at IQM, the company states.

“Joining IQM felt like a natural continuation of that journey,” Ciesla stated, “Because curiosity is everywhere here.” IQM’s commitment to building a complete quantum computing ecosystem, coupled with its emphasis on practical application and a culture of innovation, positions the company as a leader in this rapidly evolving field. “The challenge now isn’t simply proving the technology works, it’s scaling it,” he said, highlighting the company’s focus on translating scientific possibility into commercial reality.
